translational-equilibrium.def: The state of an object whose net force is zero (ΣF = 0, in every direction). Its velocity stays constant, which includes staying at rest.

first-law.def: Newton's first law: an object's velocity stays constant (it stays at rest or keeps moving in a straight line at the same speed) unless a nonzero net force acts on it.

inertia.def: The tendency of an object to keep its velocity. Mass measures inertia: the more mass, the harder it is to change the velocity. Inertia is not a force.

inertial-frame.def: A reference frame in which Newton's first law holds, such as the ground or a vehicle moving at constant velocity. An accelerating vehicle is a noninertial frame.
